name: freekit
description: Connect web AI chats (DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Mistral, Qwen) — or a local Ollama model — to VS Code, with a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) client for external tools and a local semantic code index

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode Freekit only reads files: writing files, running shell commands, changing git state and MCP tools stay disabled (the chat and read-only tools keep working) until you trust the folder.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Requires a local file system and an installed browser.

freekit.provider.description: The AI provider used by the chat. "auto" = try the last web provider through Chrome, then fall back automatically to local Ollama; web providers run through Chrome; `ollama` runs locally, without a browser.

freekit.ollamaModel.description: The Ollama model used by the local provider (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:7b).

freekit.aiSelectorFinder.markdownDescription: When enabled, sends a DOM snapshot to local Ollama to discover selectors when the fingerprint healer fails. Turn ON only if a provider's selectors break; analysis is capped at 60 seconds. The manual `Freekit: Repair Selectors` command can run discovery regardless of this setting.

freekit.aiFinderModel.markdownDescription: Ollama model used by the **AI selector finder** (independent of `freekit.ollamaModel`). `auto` = the best installed chat model: `gemma3:12b` when available, otherwise the first match by preference (`qwen2.5-coder` → `qwen-coder` → `qwen` → `llama` → `mistral` → any other). Embeddings models (`nomic-embed-*`, `bge-*`, …) are never used. Set a specific name (e.g. `qwen2.5-coder:7b`) to force one; when it is not installed the analysis is skipped with a warning in the log.

freekit.aiFinderTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Timeout per AI selector-analysis attempt (maximum 30s). The complete finder has a hard 60s timeout and at most two attempts.

freekit.responseTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long (milliseconds, 10000–1800000) to wait for one response from the web chat (ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/DeepSeek/Mistral). Long answers that contain a whole file (e.g. a `test.ts`) can take several minutes, so the default is 300000 (5 minutes). At expiry Freekit still makes a last-chance read of the assistant bubble and returns it when it looks like a real answer; only when nothing usable is found does the `Timeout: no stable response … after Ns.` error appear.

freekit.cdpPort.description: The CDP port Chrome is started on / connected to (default 9222).

freekit.chromePath.description: Path to Chrome/Edge (empty = automatic detection on Windows/macOS/Linux).

freekit.messageTimeoutMinutes.description: Total time budget (minutes) for one message in the agentic loop.

freekit.allowExternalPaths.markdownDescription: List of external paths Freekit may use, even though they are not open in the workspace — e.g. `Z:\home` (a WordPress install on a RaiDrive/network drive) or `D:\projects`. Both reads and writes are allowed inside them (writes still require approval), so the AI can inspect and, if you ask it to, modify that folder. Every allowed external path is logged in **Output → Freekit** as `[scope] allowed external path: <path>`; anything outside the workspace and this list is refused with `[scope] refused: <path>`.

freekit.handoffThreshold.markdownDescription: Number of tool results pasted into the **same** browser chat before starting a **new chat** with a full handoff. A large tool payload makes ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini process every later message slowly, and the accumulated context can hit the site's „Chat memory full” limit — a fresh chat keeps the paste small and fast. Raise it for long tasks (more context kept in one chat); lower it if the web app gets slow. **0** disables the handoff entirely (the chat is only restarted when the site reports a full context). Note: the handoff is never triggered for tasks that read *many* files and summarize them („read every file in src/ and summarize”), because the new chat would have to re-read everything.

freekit.chunkedWrites.markdownDescription: Splits large files into chunks so a browser chat (≈8k tokens per reply) does not truncate them. When a written file ends with a continuation marker (`// CONTINUARE`, `<!-- CONTINUARE -->`, `/* CONTINUARE */` or `# CONTINUARE`), Freekit automatically asks the model to continue with an `edit_file` that replaces the marker — repeating until the marker is gone (max **10** parts per file, logged as `[write] file <path> part K/10`).

freekit.planFirst.markdownDescription: For complex tasks, asks the model for a numbered **plan** before it executes anything. The plan is shown in the chat and counted in Output as `[plan] generated N steps`. With `freekit.autoApprovePlan` on (default) the plan is executed immediately; turn that setting off to review and accept/reject each plan first.

freekit.autoApprovePlan.markdownDescription: When on, a generated plan is shown in the chat and executed **without waiting** for approval. Turn it off to keep the plan card and approve (or reject) it manually before the AI starts writing files.

freekit.autoVerify.markdownDescription: After every file write (`write_file` / `edit_file` / `write_files`), automatically verifies the project (`astro check`, `tsc --noEmit` or the detected build/typecheck/lint script). On failure the error is **parsed and traced to its root cause** (`[diagnose] parsed: …` / `[diagnose] root cause: …`) and only a compact diagnostic is sent to the AI, together with the exact fix; the AI must answer with **one `edit_file`** (band-aid fixes — `?.` on `.map()`, `|| []`, `if (!x) return` — are rejected and re-prompted). Max **3 repair cycles**; if it still fails, the changes are rolled back automatically (**rollback** to the last verified-good state) and, when there is no verified-good state, you are told honestly that the error is still present.

enumDescriptions: Open the capture as a preview tab in the active editor group.
Open the capture in a new editor column, beside the current one (compare_visual always opens the two images side by side).
Do not open anything; the file is only saved in docs/screenshots/.
freekit.screenshotOpenMode.markdownDescription: How the `screenshot` / `compare_visual` capture is opened after it is written. **preview** = preview tab, **beside** = new editor column, **none** = only saved. After the capture Chrome is always returned to the background.

freekit.promptCheckpoints.markdownDescription: Before every message, creates a **git checkpoint** (commit `freekit-prompt:<id>` with the entire working tree) and shows the ⟲ button above the message, to return to that state (`git reset --hard`, with an automatic backup of the current state before the reset). In folders without git, the repo is initialized automatically (see `freekit.autoInitGit`).

freekit.autoInitGit.markdownDescription: If the project folder is not a git repo yet, initializes it automatically (`git init` + a minimal `.gitignore`, only if missing) on the first message, so checkpoints and the ⟲ restore button always work. Disable if you don't want Freekit to create a git repo in the project.

freekit.selectorsUrl.markdownDescription: **Raw** URL of a public GitHub Gist with `selectors.json` (same structure as the bundled one + `version`/`updated`/`changelog`). Empty = remote selectors disabled — only the selectors bundled with the extension are used. Example: `https://gist.githubusercontent.com/<user>/<id>/raw/selectors.json`

freekit.checkSelectorsOnStartup.markdownDescription: On startup, checks whether the Gist in `freekit.selectorsUrl` has a newer selector version. Rate limiting: at most once every 24 hours — the "Freekit: Update Selectors" command works anytime, on demand. Only takes effect if the URL is set.

freekit.humanTyping.markdownDescription: "Human" typing in the chat box: random delays between characters, pauses at punctuation and occasional fast bursts (anti-detect). Disabled = instant paste (`insertText`). Very long messages (over 1500 characters, e.g. attachments) are pasted directly.

freekit.humanBehavior.markdownDescription: "Human" behavior before actions: small mouse movements toward the pressed button (input box, new chat, stop) and occasional light scrolling (anti-detect).

freekit.mutationObserver.markdownDescription: Uses `MutationObserver` for fast detection (experimental — can be flaky with offscreen Chrome: JS is suspended for invisible windows). Disabled = classic 500ms polling (reliable). Recommended: `false`.

freekit.autoAcceptPopups.markdownDescription: Automatically closes consent popups (cookie / terms / "OK" / "Got it" / "Accept all"…) after a page loads and before typing in the chat. Safe matches only: visible buttons, exact acceptance texts at 3 confidence tiers ("OK" only inside dialogs); **Reject / Only necessary / Customize / Not now** texts are ignored completely.

freekit.sttLanguage.markdownDescription: Language for **voice input** (the 🎤 button in the chat): the recording is transcribed **locally, offline, with Whisper** and added to the message box. `ro-RO` = Romanian, `en-US` = English.

freekit.whisperCliPath.markdownDescription: Path to `whisper-cli` (whisper.cpp) for offline voice input. Empty = automatic detection: globalStorage (`whisper/bin`) → classic whisper.cpp locations → PATH.

freekit.whisperModelPath.markdownDescription: Path to the Whisper ggml model (e.g. `ggml-base.bin`). Empty = automatic detection: globalStorage (`whisper/models`) → next to the CLI → `whisper.cpp/models`.

freekit.whisperTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Timeout (seconds) for one Whisper transcription. On expiry, the process is stopped and the error is reported in the chat.

freekit.thinkingLevel.markdownDescription: Thinking level selected by the **chip in the composer** (Off / Low / Medium / High). Stored now and applied by the agent loop in a future release — the setting alone does not change the model behavior yet.

freekit.mcpEnabled.markdownDescription: Starts the configured **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** servers and exposes their tools to the AI agent as extra tools (`mcp_<server>_<tool>`). Servers are configured in `.vscode/mcp.json` (format `{"servers": {...}}`) or in the `freekit.mcpServers` setting. Every MCP call requires approval (automatic only with ⚡ auto-approve enabled).

freekit.mcpToolTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Timeout (seconds) for one MCP tool call (`tools/call`). On expiry, the call is reported as an error to the AI.

freekit.semanticIndex.enabled.markdownDescription: Enables **semantic code search** (the `search_semantic` tool + the index commands). The workspace is embedded locally with Ollama (`nomic-embed-text` by default) and stored as a JSON vector store in globalStorage — no new npm dependencies. Disabled = the AI falls back to `search_files`.

freekit.semanticIndex.model.markdownDescription: Ollama embedding model used for the semantic index (install with `ollama pull nomic-embed-text`). Changing it invalidates the existing index — re-run **Freekit: Index Workspace**.

freekit.semanticIndex.onSave.markdownDescription: Automatically re-indexes a file when it is **saved** (incremental — only that file's chunks are recomputed, debounced 1.5 s). Requires an existing index; does nothing if the workspace was never indexed.

freekit.semanticIndex.maxFileKb.markdownDescription: Files larger than this (in KB) are skipped when indexing (they are recorded as skipped, not embedded).

freekit.semanticIndex.topK.markdownDescription: Number of chunks returned by `search_semantic` (top-K by cosine similarity).

freekit.semanticIndex.exclude.markdownDescription: Extra directory/file **names** to exclude from indexing, on top of the built-in list (`node_modules`, `.git`, `out`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `coverage`, `venv`, `target`, lockfiles, minified files…). Example: `["fixtures", "snapshots"]`.

freekit.reporting.enabled.markdownDescription: Master switch for the **Freekit reporting server** integration. When on, the extension registers once (anonymous installation id), periodically checks that the web-AI selectors still work, tries to repair them locally first, and — only if the repair fails — reports the broken selector so a fix can be published to everyone. No code, files or messages are ever sent; disable to opt out completely.

freekit.reporting.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of the reporting server (the extension calls `/api/v1/extensions/register`, `/api/v1/selectors` and `/api/v1/reports` under it). Change it only for self-hosted servers or testing.

freekit.reporting.shareDomSnapshot.markdownDescription: When reporting a broken selector, also send a **cleaned DOM snapshot** of the page (scripts, styles, media and input values are stripped, truncated to a few thousand characters). It makes fixing the selector far easier, but it does send a fragment of the page's HTML — off by default.

freekit.reporting.healthCheck.markdownDescription: Periodically verifies the selectors of providers that **already have a tab open** in the Freekit Chrome profile. Missing selectors are repaired locally (fingerprint + AI finder) first; only if that also fails is a report sent. Chrome is never started just for this check.

freekit.reporting.healthCheckIntervalHou.markdownDescription: Hours between two automatic selector health checks (default **6**). The first check runs shortly after startup.

freekit.reporting.selectorsIntervalHours.markdownDescription: Hours between two automatic fetches of repaired selectors from the server (default **24**). Newly received selectors are applied immediately and used on the next message.
